Name:
Since I Left You II
(Since I Left II)
Notes:
Version renamed to "Since I Left You II" (or Since I Left II), released on February 10th, 2011. This version has 17 tracks, most of them with names that are unique to this version specifically (although Devon's Tape might've also used these names). Description for the album reads:

"In the year 2000 a group of australian Dj's the Avalanches released Since I left you on Modular Records. Comprised almost entirely of old records. Since I Left You flowed with momentum of it was masterpiece of mood-setting & there wasn't a single misstep. The Word Classic is tossed around often in music industry. But, this is more than a "classic" Since I left You is a record that remains frozen in time...as the world around it moves forward. Since The release of Since I left You, The Avalanches have remained silent only releasing scarce details of a follow up album. Then in 2011 rapper Devon Hendryx took the matter into his own hands, and vowed to do what the The Avlanches Have not.....Deliver a follow up to a classic. This album unlike the first is dark, cold, and lonely. Submerged in Sonar pings liquid feedback bright echos DeVon effortlessly makes a sequel that is massive, glacial, and sparse & once youv'e completely tuned in, It fascinates you more and more with each listen."

Name: JOECHILLWORLD [DatPiff Upload]
Notes: Version uploaded to DatPiff. There was likely an error when uploading this version, as all audio files—with the exception of Sabbath School—are corrupted and feature some sort of skip. Most songs simply skip a few seconds of audio around the middle to the end of the song, Montebello High School Prom specifically cuts to an unidentified trap beat for around 20 seconds then returns to normal.

Name: JOECHILLWORLD [V3]
Notes: Third version, Sabbath School has been shortened, slowed, and no longer features a verse. Has short monologue near the end and transitions into Bully. Neon Kitchen fades back in at the end. Re: Neon Kitchen has been renamed to "Neon Kitchen II". Game of the Century is slightly longer due to a short clip of maniacal laughing being added at the beginning. 1989 (Michelle's Song) has been added to the end, but was notably hidden on the Bandcamp page, you could not see it unless you downloaded the album. Album cover now features a Parental Advisory logo in the bottom right corner, which is higher quality than the entire rest of the image.

Name: JOECHILLWORLD [V4]
Notes: Fourth version. This release is the most well-known, featuring Enso Sinatra (aka DATPIFFMEDIA) in the iconic Iron Man mask as the album cover. The entire album has been newly mixed and mastered. Many songs no longer feature beat cuts and most instances of background vocals or adlibs have been shortened or removed entirely. Sabbath School is now back at normal speed, but is still instrumental aside from the short monologue. This version transitions into Bully in a different way. Neon Kitchen has been shortened by nearly a minute. Trophy Kids is 10 seconds shorter and no longer features rain noises. Omega Weapon no longer features 30 seconds of a droning noise at the beginning. Montebello High School Prom features a slightly different arrangement and is noticably faster. The Power of Madonna no longer fades out at the end, and now transitions into the next track. Game of the Century has been shortened to just the 40 seconds of whistling at the end, and has been renamed to "Blue Seed". 1989 (Michelle's Song) has been removed.

Name: JOECHILLWORLD [V5]
Notes: Version with the songs "Bully" & "Neon Kitchen II", being censored to remove some slurs (notably the word "white"). This is the version available on his Bandcamp, as well as streaming.

Name: JOECHILLWORLD (+)
Notes: Trashfuck Records reissue, pretty much just the initial release mixed in with the third version (or just the initial release with 1989 (I Used To Know Her) added).

Name: The Rockwood Escape Plan [V1]
Notes: Initial release. Toonami features vocals, including a full verse as well as monologue sections. Includes "☁✈" as the final track, exclusive to this release. "I ♥ You Hip Hop But I Can't Be Your Girlfriend Because That's Gay" featured on this release is the longest version of the track to use the original beat.

Name: The Rockwood Escape Plan [V2]
Notes: Second version, released in July 2012. I ♥ You Hip Hop But I Can't Be Your Girlfriend Because That's Gay has been shortened. Y2K is longer, and is now before Sunday School in the tracklist. Sunday School is now subtitled "Church of Granas" and is 33 seconds longer. A short interlude titled "2004年9月9日" was added and is placed after The 27 Club. Toonami has been shortened and no longer features vocals. ☁✈ has been removed. Multiple songs now credit features in their titles, but most of them are fake, with the only real ones being Enso Sinatra on A Song About Nothing and Rebecca on Generation Y 1989. As with his update to JOECHILLWORLD around the same time, the cover has been updated to include a Parental Advisory logo in the bottom right corner.

Name: The Rockwood Escape Plan [V3]
Notes: Third version. The entire album has been newly mixed and mastered. Many songs no longer feature beat cuts and most instances of background vocals or adlibs have been shortened or removed entirely. I ♥ You Hip Hop But I Can't Be Your Girlfriend Because That's Gay has been completely reproduced, with an entirely new beat replacing the original. Quisha has been significantly shortened and is over 2 minutes shorter than previous versions. Archives of the album page suggest this was a small update that happened prior to this full album update, it is featured here due to its continued prescence on this copy. God & Earrings is now shorter and has a slightly different arrangement. MissingNo. features 10 extra seconds of silence at the end, followed by a seemingly random noise. Pu$$y has been renamed to "Pu$$y #1", likely to correspond with the then-recent full release of Pu$$y #3. Y2K has been restructured and no longer features vocals. Neon Kitchen III and 2004年9月9日 have been removed. The outro of The 27 Club has been shortened and split off as its own track, titled "DIP". Generation Y 1989 no longer contains high-pitched adlibs. Feature credits have been removed, except for A Song About Nothing and MissingNo.

Name: The Rockwood EP
Notes: Version with only the last 8 tracks, released in 2015 on cassette by Granola Records. This release was made because according to Peggy, "...the album actually ends on track 15 "Pu$$y #1" i think and the rest of it is a completely seperate project that i put on the end because the tracks were recorded so far apart that i had to many songs". Reissued in 2022 - 2023 on cassette & vinyl by Trashfuck Records, but has no differences.

Name: The Rockwood Escape Plan [V4]
Notes: Version with "Deuce Komradz" being censored to remove both slurs & personal information respectively. I ♥ You Hip Hop But I Can't Be Your Girlfriend Because That's Gay has been renamed to simply "I ♥ You Hip Hop But I Can't Be Your Girlfriend", & the title of "Hoe$" has been removed, leaving it with just its subtitle. This is the version available on his Bandcamp, as well as streaming.

Name: GenY⁵
Notes: Initial release, exported sometime between August 16th & September 3rd, 2013 (although the latter is likely correct) & released under the psuedonym "geny⁸⁹". Was available exclusively on geny89.com. This version has 20 tracks, "Porn for Percussion" (titled "[Missing image file_ maladaptivedaydreaming.gif]" on this version) is an alternate version from other copies, and would later be included on the Expanded Edition as "Porn for Percussion (Betamax Version)". Includes the instrumental for Black Materia as the outro, the track is exclusive to this version. This version in particular was reissued onto CD by Trashfuck Records.

Name:
GHOST~POP OST
(THE GHOST~POP TAPE)
Notes: Second version, released under the name "GHOST~POP OST" and under the artist name GHOST~POP on the ghostpop.jp website. Untitled² has its title misspelled in comparison to the previous version. This would be not be fixed until 2014, and would then also be present on the Ben Yuddha version. Omits Black Materia, but otherwise the tracklist is identical to GenY⁵. Album cover is completely unique to this version, however new versions of the album include a png for the cover in the download. Had its cover changed to the final cover and was renamed to THE GHOST~POP TAPE shortly after release, as indicated by a review of the album from November 2013. Due to the mention of there being 19 tracks, it can be presumed that no other alterations had been made to the album at that point besides this. Download provided by ZenDash.

Name: THE GHOST~POP TAPE [V1]
Notes: Third version. HBK is named "HBK Fsharp CHROM". Porn for Percussion and [Missing image file_ maladaptivedaydreaming.gif] have switched names, a change that is never reversed. Porn for Percussion is now the fully produced version heard in the movie, replacing the guitar-based version from previous copies. Unititled² has added kick drums to the end of the song. This version would much later become the basis for the remastered version of the song. Bubblegum Crisis now features a snippet of LIARA at the end of the song. LIARA is also added to the tracklist in this version. ODB has a crowd intro, which is not present on earlier versions of the album but is shorter than the one from the medley. Features yet another album cover that would go on to be used in basically every version of the album after this.

Name: THE GHOST~POP TAPE [V2]
Notes: Fourth version, considered the "standard version" since most of the tracks on this version would not be altered on major releases past this besides the remaster. Most physical releases (barring the remastered ones) are based off this version. [Missingimagefile_ maladaptivedaydreaming.gif] has had additional vocals near the beginning removed. Untitled² has been changed once again, the drop no longer changes keys and has different kicks. Is also slightly shorter. Untitled³ now includes a long period of silence at the end, followed by multiple text-to-speech voices saying "The ghost pop tape is over". ODB's crowd intro is now identical to the medley's, including the talking. ODB and Sakura are no longer main tracklist songs, and have been moved to a second disc. Includes the booklet and the trailer for the movie as part of the download. Was hosted on Dropbox and was still available to download until ~2018 - 2019 when he began to delete a lot of his old downloads and videos. The files linked below are MP3s, an M4A version was hosted alongside it but seemingly nobody downloaded it before it was deleted.

Name: THE GHOST~POP TAPE [V3]
Notes: Version identical to the one above, except it excludes ODB and Sakura from the tracklist altogether. Was hosted on both the Devon Hendryx Bandcamp and a new GHOST~POP Bandcamp (the original was renamed to ghostpop1). The GHOST~POP page had all titles in Japanese and excluded the number from "Neon Kitchen⁴". Neither page hosted a download, both were only playable on the page itself. Was finally made available to download in mid-2019, mere months before the release of the Expanded Edition.

Name:
Ben Yuddha
(THE GHOST~POP TAPE [V4])
Notes: Ben Yuddha was yet another alias of his, with the only surviving things attributed to it being his current Reddit account and Internet Archive captures of this old Bandcamp account and a separate website. Nobody knew it existed until late 2023 when it would be found by member of the community Aviant, who simply stumbled upon it while searching things on Internet Archive. The name on the page would eventually be changed to Darkskin Manson, and then finally to JPEGMAFIA, which it continues as today. The only evidence of this page's existence prior to this were scrobbles on Last.fm from 2015 attributing the tracks to Darkskin Manson. The page seems to host a unique version of the album, with all tracks released individually as singles, each with their own covers. When asked about this copy, Zen Dash stated that this copy might've just been unedited demos. Included two potentially unheard songs, "God" (which might be related to the YouTube single of the same name) & "AJ Lee". Zen Dash thinks these are previously released singles, with AJ Lee being an old song under a new name. Track durations are significantly longer than any other version of the album. As evidenced by the lyrics, "Porn for Percussion [Betamax Version]" is not the song found on the Expanded Edition, but rather is a retitled "[Missingimagefile_ maladaptivedaydreaming.gif]". Neon Kitchen⁴ is simply titled "Neon Kitchen".

Name: THE GHOST~POP TAPE [V5]
Notes: Version released in June 2015 on cassette by Granola Records. Contains the full 18-track tracklisting with the only difference being an "extended" version of Porn for Percussion (using both the VCR & Betamax version, which won't be added because technically it's unofficial), as well as four bonus tracks: ODB, Piano Baby, Sakura & Pardon Me Michelle. These files have encoding either from Peggy or the owner of Granola Records.

Name: THE GHOST~POP TAPE [V6]
Notes: Expanded version with extra bonus tracks, released more than 6 years after the album's original release. The main 18 tracks of the standard version are almost fully intact, with 7 bonus tracks now being part of a continuous tracklist, rather than a second disc. The included bonus tracks are "ODB", "Piano Baby", "Sakura", "Pardon Me Michael (Demo)", "Pizzicato Five", "BBTG (2011 Demo)", and "Porn for Percussion (Betamax Version)". Untitled³ no longer includes the text-to-speech voices and simply ends after silence. ODB has been cut early due to the inclusion of Piano Baby, which it now transitions into. ODB also features extremely loud crackling for seemingly no reason, no other release of the song sounded like this and it has not yet been fixed. Sakura is completely unchanged. Pardon Me Michael (Demo) uses Silver St. Cloud for its instrumental. Pizzicato Five is identical to the version on ♥ and the single version. Porn for Percussion (Betamax Version) is the same as the main version found on GenY⁵ and GHOST~POP OST.
